reading.title: Finding the Way Across Land and Sea
reading.purpose: Learn how travelers plan long journeys and steer safely through unfamiliar places.
paras: For a long time, people have set out on big trips to map new coasts, trade goods, or watch wildlife. A team may plan a land expedition into thick woods or a sea voyage over wide water. Either way, smart plans keep everyone safe.

First, travelers pick a clear destination, the place they hope to reach. Before they leave, they study maps of the terrain. Those maps show whether the land is flat, rocky, or steep. Crossing a hot desert often takes a caravan, a group of travelers moving as one so they can share water and food.

Once a trip begins, travelers must navigate, steering along the right path even when landmarks fade. At sea or in deep woods, a compass helps because its needle always points north. Sailors also watch the sun and stars to check their way.

Some trips mean leaving towns behind to enter the wilderness, a wild place where few people live. Hikers may trek for days on foot over wet trails and high hills. When they venture into risky spots, they pack extra food, warm coats, and a spare map.
Good tools and steady teamwork turn a hard trip into a safe find.

choices: a tool with a needle that points north
a group of travelers moving together
a natural place where few people live
a flat, rocky, or steep stretch of land
qs.why: Paragraph 2 defines a caravan as "a group of travelers moving together so they can share water and supplies."

qs.q: Which sentence explains how a compass helps travelers?
choices: Once a trip begins, travelers must navigate, steering along the right path even when landmarks vanish.
At sea or in deep woods, a compass helps because its needle always points north.
Sailors also watch the sun and stars to check their direction.
Good tools and steady teamwork turn a hard journey into a safe discovery.
qs.why: This sentence tells why a compass is useful: its needle always points north.

ev.text: At sea or in deep woods, a compass helps because its needle always points north.

qs.q: Why do desert travelers often move in a caravan instead of traveling alone?
choices: They can share water and supplies on the long trip.
They want to sail across open water in one large boat together.
They do not need maps of the terrain when they travel in a group.
They can avoid packing warm coats or backup maps for the desert.
qs.why: Paragraph 2 says travelers cross a wide desert in a caravan so they can share water and supplies.

qs.q: What is the main idea of this reading?
choices: Only sailors who watch the stars at night know how to navigate safely.
Walking through snowy ridges is safer than crossing a wide desert.
Planning, tools, and teamwork help travelers finish hard journeys safely.
Every science expedition must cross a rainforest before reaching its goal.
qs.why: The reading explains how travelers plan destinations, study terrain, use compasses, and pack smartly to stay safe.
